evidence_scope: Pinned language and lint documentation; curated conditional mechanisms, not verified target bugs or historical bug-fix pairs.

records.scope_note: Refines the multiplicity branch of this card only. A repeated literal hiding a missing distinct entry needs separate specification evidence.

requirements.text: The observable must retain repeated occurrences or their counts.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote a public requirement distinguishing counts from distinct membership.

requirements.text: Equal values may occur more than once in an admissible input.
requirements.required_evidence: Public input restrictions permit duplicates; absence of a restriction alone remains unknown.

requirements.text: The deduplicated value reaches a count-sensitive decision or output without recovering multiplicity.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for set construction, value flow and the affected consumer.

records.effect: Equal occurrences collapse to one set member, erasing multiplicity.
records.consumer: Occurrence count, repeated-item output or matching logic requiring distinct uses of equal occurrences.
records.trigger: Choose two admissible collections with identical distinct members and different occurrence counts, for which the contract requires different results.
exclusions: The contract asks only for distinct membership or cardinality.
Original counts remain available and the consumer uses them.
The admissible domain guarantees uniqueness.
records.benign_contrast: Counting distinct values with len(set(values)) satisfies a distinct-cardinality contract; this is a conceptual contrast, not an executed target example.

citations.quote: A :dfn:`set` object is an unordered collection of distinct :term:`hashable` objects.
citations.supports: Set uniqueness semantics, not the target's need for occurrence counts.

realizations: one stored state per value used as remaining occurrences
records.scope_note: These realizations share information loss; their concrete state transitions must still be inspected separately.

requirements.text: The public result distinguishes occurrence counts or requires each occurrence to be consumed once.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote the multiplicity or distinct-occurrence requirement.

requirements.text: The relevant state stores membership or one position while losing required remaining-count information.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for state initialization, updates and reads; a dictionary may store counts and is not inherently insufficient.

requirements.text: The input domain allows enough repeated values to distinguish presence from count.
requirements.required_evidence: Public domain restriction and admissible repeated-value input class.

records.effect: Presence records whether an occurrence exists; it cannot by itself distinguish one, two and three remaining occurrences.
records.consumer: Frequency comparison, repeated-item output or pairing that must not reuse a consumed occurrence.
records.trigger: Vary multiplicity while preserving distinct members; for toggled presence also compare two and three occurrences, subject to the contract.
exclusions: Only existence or parity is required.
A separate counter or occurrence list supplies the information.
The domain guarantees unique values.
records.benign_contrast: Membership is sufficient for an existence query even when duplicates occur; no target execution is claimed.

citations.quote: The operators :keyword:`in` and :keyword:`not in` test for membership.
citations.supports: Membership semantics; insufficiency for a specific target remains a conditional inference.

realizations: encoded byte measurement substitutes for character measurement
records.scope_note: Code points, grapheme clusters and bytes are distinct domains; the intended domain must be explicit.

requirements.text: The public contract measures or accepts text characters, with the relevant character unit identified.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote the unit and accepted character-domain requirement; do not infer it solely from a function name.

requirements.text: Encoding affects a returned measurement, a decision, or an exception visible to the caller.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for encoding and its consumer or propagating exception path.

requirements.text: Admissible text distinguishes the selected encoding from the required character domain.
requirements.required_evidence: Public restrictions permit the proposed characters and the selected encoding is resolved.

records.effect: Encoding changes the representation to bytes and can raise an encoding error; character-level observations need not be preserved.
records.consumer: Length, indexing, distinct-character measurement or successful processing of admissible text.
records.trigger: Use contract-admissible characters with multiple bytes in the selected encoding, or characters it cannot encode; choose the case matching the actual consumer.
exclusions: The contract explicitly counts encoded bytes.
The admissible encoding/domain is known to preserve the required observation.
Encoded bytes only feed a byte-oriented consumer such as hashing with the required encoding.
records.benign_contrast: Computing payload size in encoded bytes is appropriate when the API specifies byte length; this is a conceptual contrast.

citations.quote: If ``'strict'`` (the default), a :exc:`UnicodeError` exception is raised.
citations.supports: Documented handling when an encoding error occurs; not proof that a particular input causes one.

realizations: return or break after first eligible candidate without establishing optimality
records.scope_note: Eligibility, optimum and tie policy are separate requirements; returning the first tied optimum can be correct.

requirements.text: The contract requires a minimum, maximum or closest eligible candidate, not merely any or first candidate.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote eligibility, ordering key and tie policy from the public contract.

requirements.text: Selection stops at an eligible candidate before considering a potentially better eligible candidate.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for traversal order, eligibility check and exit; inspect sorting or monotonicity guarantees.

requirements.text: An admissible traversal can place a worse eligible candidate before a better one.
requirements.required_evidence: Public ordering restrictions and actual traversal permit the proposed order.

records.effect: Existence of an eligible candidate is substituted for optimality over all eligible candidates.
records.consumer: Returned selected value, object or position.
records.trigger: Place a worse eligible candidate before a better eligible candidate in the actual traversal order; derive the expected choice from the public key and tie rule.
exclusions: The contract requests the first or any eligible match.
Traversal is guaranteed to visit the best eligible candidate first.
An admissible domain has at most one eligible candidate.
records.benign_contrast: Early return after sorting by the required key can be correct if eligibility and tie rules are preserved; no target proof is implied.

citations.quote: Return the largest item in an iterable or the largest of two or more arguments.
citations.supports: Maximum semantics used to explain the optimum requirement; not evidence of an early-exit bug.

citations.quote: If multiple items are maximal, the function returns the first one encountered.
citations.supports: First occurrence is valid for tied builtin maxima.

realizations: fixed initial maximum exceeds all eligible values
fixed initial minimum is below all eligible values
records.scope_note: The sentinel is problematic only when the contract requires an eligible value and an admissible path leaves it selected.

requirements.text: For a nonempty eligible collection the result must select its required extremum.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote selection semantics and any empty-case or sentinel policy.

requirements.text: A fixed initialization survives when no eligible candidate passes the comparison update, and it reaches the output.
requirements.required_evidence: Same-value provenance through initialization, comparison update and consumer.

requirements.text: All eligible candidates may lie below the initial maximum or above the initial minimum.
requirements.required_evidence: Public domain bounds permit the entire candidate collection on that side of the sentinel.

records.effect: An artificial initialization remains selected instead of an eligible extremum.
records.consumer: Returned extremum or the object/index attached to the accumulator.
records.trigger: Use one or several eligible values all beyond the sentinel on the non-updating side; inspect comparison direction and equality handling.
exclusions: The sentinel is a valid extremal bound for the admitted domain and first-candidate handling is correct.
The contract explicitly allows this sentinel for this case.
Initialization comes from an eligible candidate and updates maintain the required optimum.
records.benign_contrast: A zero maximum initializer can be valid when the contract guarantees nonnegative values and the returned value satisfies selection requirements; index/object outputs need additional checks.

citations.quote: The largest item in the iterable is returned.
citations.supports: Eligible-extremum semantics; the sentinel failure is a curated conditional deduction.

realizations: filter removes every candidate before min or max without a default
records.scope_note: Nonempty original input does not establish nonempty filtered input; not all reducers reject empty input.

requirements.text: The contract admits an input with no eligible candidates and requires a result rather than the observed reduction exception.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote input admissibility and empty-candidate result or exception policy.

requirements.text: An empty derived iterable reaches a resolved min or max without a suitable default or handling.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for the filter, reaching iterable, builtin resolution and absent handling on the path.

requirements.text: An admissible input can make every element fail eligibility.
requirements.required_evidence: Eligibility condition and public domain allow an all-rejected collection.

records.effect: The reducer's nonempty-domain requirement is violated after filtering.
records.consumer: The reduction call and the caller-visible return or exception.
records.trigger: Use admissible input whose elements all fail the actual filter; include a nonempty original collection when allowed to distinguish input guards from derived-domain guards.
exclusions: Public contract permits the reduction exception in this case.
A guard checks the same stable derived iterable.
A suitable default or exception handler implements the required empty-case behavior.
The domain guarantees at least one eligible candidate.
records.benign_contrast: An empty sum returning zero is not evidence for the min/max empty-domain mechanism; reducer identity must be resolved.

citations.quote: If the iterable is empty and *default* is not provided, a :exc:`ValueError` is raised.
citations.supports: Builtin min/max empty-input behavior, not target input reachability or expected policy.

records.scope_note: The citation directly documents lower/lstrip; each other normalization operation needs its own resolved semantics before application.

requirements.text: The required observable distinguishes case or content changed by this normalization.
requirements.required_evidence: Quote the preservation or case-sensitive comparison requirement.

requirements.text: A normalized value influences the observable without restoring the required distinction.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for the resolved transformation and output/decision consumer.

requirements.text: Admissible inputs differ in a distinction erased by this transformation.
requirements.required_evidence: Public character and whitespace restrictions permit the contrast.

records.effect: Different original texts become indistinguishable to a consumer that must distinguish them.
records.consumer: Case-sensitive comparison, preserved output text or significant-character measurement.
records.trigger: Choose admissible texts that normalize alike but require different outputs; select case, whitespace or removed characters according to the actual operation.
exclusions: The public contract explicitly ignores or normalizes the distinction.
Only a normalization-invariant classification is consumed.
The original value supplies the required observable.
records.benign_contrast: Lowercasing before a case-insensitive membership comparison can meet its contract; lowercasing alone is not bug evidence.

citations.quote: Return a copy of the string with all the cased characters [4]_ converted to lowercase.
Return a copy of the string with leading characters removed.
citations.supports: lstrip transformation semantics, not every text-normalization API.

realizations: mutating a shared function-argument default across omitted-argument calls
records.scope_note: The pinned Python FAQ supplies both the failure illustration and intentional memoization contrast; these are documentation examples, not mined historical fixes.

requirements.text: Calls that omit this argument must not inherit semantically relevant state from earlier calls.
requirements.required_evidence: Public independence or fresh-state requirement; do not infer it solely from mutability.

requirements.text: Calls mutate and later observe the same definition-time default object.
requirements.required_evidence: Source spans for default creation, omitted-argument binding, mutations and later reads; account for reset or copy behavior.

requirements.text: Repeated omitted-argument calls in the same function lifetime are admissible.
requirements.required_evidence: Public call/lifecycle contract allows the call sequence.

records.effect: State persists in the definition-time object and changes later independent-call behavior.
records.consumer: Later returned value or externally visible side effect affected by the shared object.
records.trigger: Make two admissible calls omitting the mutable argument; compare the second observable with the contractually equivalent fresh-state call, accounting for return aliasing.
exclusions: Shared state is an intentional cache and preserves all required observables.
The default is not mutated or mutation cannot affect later observables.
A fresh copy or reset occurs before every relevant use.
records.benign_contrast: The Python FAQ explicitly demonstrates memoization with a mutable default cache; shared state can be intentional.

citations.quote: Default values are created exactly once, when the function is defined.

citations.supports: The following FAQ memoization example is an intentional shared-state use, not a bug-fix commit.
